diagnostic_evidence.quote: there exist constants $A_{\ell}<2$, $B_{\ell}>2$ such that for any given $h>0$
Since the process $X$ has finite moments of all orders up to $k\in\mathbb{N}$  if and only if  $\int_{\left\Vert z\right\Vert >\epsilon}e^{k\left\Vert z\right\Vert }\ell\left(dz\right)<\infty$

issues.failure_explanation: The text asserts that finiteness of moments of X is equivalent to $\int e^{k\|z\|}\ell(dz)<\infty$ and that $k<B_\ell$ (resp. $B_\ell\ge 2$) is a necessary condition. In fact the k-th moment of $X^{(i)}=X^{(i)}(0)e^{L^{(i)}}$ requires only $\int e^{k z^{(i)}}\ell(dz)<\infty$ (one-sided, coordinate-wise), and an isotropic bound $\ell=O(e^{-B_\ell\|z\|})$ with $k<B_\ell$ is merely sufficient, not necessary. Moreover, the paper's own formula $B_\ell=\sqrt{\|\eta\|_\rho^2+2\lambda}-\|\eta\|_\rho$ evaluated at the VG0 parameters ($\lambda=1$, $\rho=[[0.09,0.06],[0.06,0.16]]$, $\eta=(-0.1,-0.2)$, giving $\|\eta\|_\rho^2\approx0.259$) yields $B_\ell\approx1.50-0.51\approx0.99<2$, so the VG0 experiment violates the paper's standing assumption $B_\ell>2$ (finite variance of X does hold for VG0 via the coordinate exponential-moment condition, which is the correct criterion).

failure_location.quote:
then $k<B_\ell$  provides a necessary condition of it. Following \citet[Chapter 6]{applebaum2004}, the stronger condition $B_{\ell}\geq2$ is necessary to guarantee the
existence of a unique solution with finite variance

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the moment discussion with the correct statement (coordinate-wise exponential-moment condition; $k<B_\ell$ is sufficient), and either relax the standing assumption on $B_\ell$ accordingly or note explicitly that VG0 violates $B_\ell>2$ yet satisfies the finite-variance condition.
issues.overall_effect: The stated scope/hypotheses of the model framework are inconsistent with the numerical experiments: one of the four test cases falls outside the announced assumptions, and the discussion of what B_l guarantees is logically inverted (sufficient stated as necessary).
issues.title: Exponential-decay assumption B_l>2 mischaracterized as necessary and violated by the VG0 test set
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the hypothesis statement suffices; no numerical result or method is affected, since the correct finite-variance condition holds for all parameter sets.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let $T^{\text{in}}\in\mathbb{R}^{\left(\sharp\text{in}\right)^{2}\times\left(N_{x}+1\right)^{2}}$
be a matrix representing an interpolation procedure from the $\mathbf{x}$
grid to the $\mathbf{y}^{\text{in}}$ grid
Interpolation is performed by cubic Lagrange polynomials.

issues.failure_explanation: The interpolation matrices act between 2-dimensional tensor-product grids (rows indexed by $(m_1,m_2)$). Tensor-product Lagrange interpolation of degree $P$ in each direction uses $(P+1)^2$ stencil points per target point (16 for cubic), not $P+1$; the operation count is $O(MP^2)$, not $O(MP)$.

failure_location.quote:
the interpolation matrices
are sparse and have at most $P+1$ nonzero entries per row, where
$P$ is the polynomial degree. Let $M$ be the number of rows, it
follows that the corresponding matrix--vector multiplications require
a number of operations of order $O\left(MP\right)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State $(P+1)^2$ nonzeros per row and cost $O(MP^2)$.
issues.overall_effect: The stated per-row sparsity and cost of $T^{in}$, $T^{out}$, $T^{SL}$ are incorrect by a factor $P+1$; the qualitative conclusion that interpolation is negligible relative to the FFT still holds.
issues.title: Sparsity count of 2-D Lagrange interpolation matrices understated
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of a constant factor; all guarantees and conclusions about efficiency survive.

issues.failure_explanation: By subordination, $\mathbb{V}[B(G(1))]=\mathbb{E}[G(1)]\rho+\mathbb{V}[G(1)]\eta\eta^\top=\delta\Gamma(2-\alpha)\lambda^{-(2-\alpha)}(\rho\lambda/(1-\alpha)+\eta\eta^\top)$, which is the appendix formula. The Section 4 display replaces $\lambda/(1-\alpha)$ by $\lambda^{1-\alpha}$; the two agree only for $\alpha=0$. For NIG0 ($\alpha=1/2$) the Section 4 formula gives $\sqrt{\mathbb{V}[L^{(1)}(1)]}\approx0.021$ whereas the appendix formula gives $\approx0.1958$, matching Table 2, so the Section 4 formula is the wrong one.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\rho\lambda^{1-\alpha}$ by $\rho\lambda/(1-\alpha)$ in the Section 4 display.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed variance formula in the experiments section is false for $\alpha\ne0$; tabulated standard deviations and correlations are nevertheless consistent with the correct appendix formula.
issues.title: Variance formula for the NTS process in Section 4 is inconsistent with the appendix and with the tabulated values
issues.why_classification: Local correction of one formula; the correct version is present elsewhere in the paper and the numerical tables already use it.
